question: A team member is worried that connecting Google Drive will let colleagues read files they are not allowed to open. What is accurate?
options: A) A connector requires every file to be made public in Drive before Claude is able to read any of them.
B) A connector gives everyone in the workspace the same view, so the file permissions no longer apply inside Claude.
C) A connector follows each person's existing permissions, so files they cannot open in Drive stay out of reach.
D) A connector copies the files into a shared store, so anyone in the organisation can search them later.
correct_answers: C) A connector follows each person's existing permissions, so files they cannot open in Drive stay out of reach.
explanations: No change to a file's sharing settings is required to use a connector.
Connectors do not flatten or override the permissions of the connected service.
Correct. If someone cannot reach a file in the source system, the connector cannot reach it for them either.
Connectors read from the source system rather than duplicating files into a shared pool.
